name: CONDITIONING CHAMBER
desc: Fully Automatic Rectangular Laboratory Conditioning Chamber engineered for pre-test and post-test sample environmental conditioning across testing industries. Features a high-capacity 225 liter (8.0 cubic feet) internal working chamber fabricated from high-grade polished SS.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS Conditioning Chamber is a fully automatic microprocessor-controlled environmental stabilization system engineered to create and maintain precise temperature and humidity conditions for pre-test and post-test conditioning of raw materials and finished specimens. It operates by circulating heated air and controlled moisture injection within a 225-liter mirror-finish stainless steel chamber, enabling uniform exposure of samples to standardized atmospheres. This chamber is widely used by textile technologists, paper scientists, polymer chemists, and PhD researchers to condition hygroscopic materials such as cotton, wool, paper, cellulose, nylon, PET, and rubber compounds under ISO 139, ISO 187, ASTM D618, and ASTM D1349. It supports moisture-sensitive pharmaceutical stability studies, accelerated aging of plastic polymers, and evaluation of volatile organic compound (VOC) emission from cured resins, adhesives, and coatings. Doctors and clinical researchers may use it for conditioning diagnostic reagents, culture media, or medical packaging materials under controlled humidity to prevent degradation. The integrated PID controller continuously compares chamber sensor feedback with setpoints and modulates heaters and humidification to maintain stability within ±2°C and ±3% RH, ensuring reproducible conditioning for B.Sc/M.Sc students, chemists, and industrial quality control laboratories.
sop: Verify that the chamber is clean, the three perforated SS trays are properly seated, and the power cord is connected to a 220-240 V AC, 50 Hz single-phase supply.
Switch ON the mains isolator and the chamber power switch; allow the microprocessor-based controller to complete its self-diagnostic routine.
Open the heavy-duty door using the ergonomic handle and load test specimens (textiles, paper, polymers, rubber, etc.) onto the trays with at least 2 cm spacing for uniform air circulation.
Close the door firmly and engage the built-in key lock to ensure a sealed chamber environment.
Press the 'SET' button once to enter the temperature setpoint mode.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target parameter (e.g., 22°C ± 2°C for ambient conditioning or up to 450°C for accelerated aging).
Press 'SET' again to lock the value.
Press the 'SET' button once more to enter the humidity setpoint mode (if available on the controller).
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target parameter (e.g., 65% ± 3% RH for standard textile/paper conditioning or 40-75% RH for specific assays).
Press 'SET' again to lock the value.

Allow the chamber to stabilize for at least 30-60 minutes; monitor the digital display and use the transparent viewing window with internal illumination to confirm uniform conditioning without opening the door.
After the conditioning period, switch OFF the heaters and humidity injection, allow the chamber to cool to near ambient, then open the door and remove samples using heat-resistant gloves.

Safety Warning: Never open the chamber door during high-temperature operation or active humidity injection; always wear heat-resistant gloves and safety goggles, and ensure that samples do not emit flammable or toxic VOCs at the set temperature, as this may cause fire or exposure hazards.
